# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platforms: iPhone and Apple TV. Current prototype requires reading a long tutorial before play, uses color-only tiles and assumes touch dragging on every device. Losing forces a purchase screen. Sessions should be short and resumable.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.
3. For device changes such as opening an iPhone Duo or resizing an iPad window, specify what selection, editing state and route survive each transition.
4. Deliver a platform-decision matrix or an adaptation patch, with concrete acceptance scenarios for each materially different interaction.

# Apple HIG: Map user actions to input and alternatives

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the action and available hardware/input context, then enter the keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controller, Pencil, Crown or sensor procedure.
2. Preserve reserved system gestures and familiar input meanings. Separate targeting, focus, selection and activation; define feedback and reachable alternatives for the actions people must complete.
3. Account for comfort, precision, fatigue and switching between available inputs. Custom inputs should not remove an accessible route to an essential action.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

# Make television choices visible from across the room

Read [Designing for tvOS](../../references/designing-for-tvos.md). Inspect the primary activity, content hierarchy, viewer/profile model, authentication, and input assumptions. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and use supplied evidence to separate confirmed defects from untested remote behavior.

Rebuild the hierarchy around distant viewing and focus navigation. Prioritize legible titles and recognizable imagery rather than filling the TV with desktop density. Map directional movement and selection from each major region. The focused item must visibly identify both location and the available action through the platform's focus treatment; do not leave essential navigation dependent on pointer hover or tiny touch targets.

Choose the appropriate input contract. Siri Remote must support ordinary browsing; games may add controllers and relevant companion/voice input. Avoid making controller possession necessary for non-controller tasks. For long sessions or picture-in-picture, preserve the person's place when attention changes.

Reduce repetitive authentication using appropriate system integration. If the current system viewer changes, switch to the matching app profile deliberately and preserve privacy boundaries. Add Top Shelf, TV-app discovery, provider support, or SharePlay only when the content/activity warrants it, with a destination that matches the selected item.

**Before → decision → after:** A cooking-video app uses small tab labels, pointer hover menus, and one permanently signed-in household profile. Decision: across-room remote browsing and changing viewers require explicit focus routes and profile ownership. After, clear focusable categories lead into large recipe artwork, Select starts the highlighted recipe, and a viewer change updates saved recipes instead of exposing another person's history.

Deliver a focus-route map and corrected screen/profile flow or implementation. Fail if focus is invisible, a region has no remote exit, or a viewer change retains another profile's personal content. Check actual remote traversal, television legibility, and focus enlargement on supported hardware; a desktop screenshot only supports visual hypotheses.

For detailed movement use [Focus and selection](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) and [Remotes](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md); for shared viewing use [SharePlay](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-shareplay/SKILL.md).

description: Use when designing, reviewing, or porting a game across Apple platforms, including first play, display adaptation, input alternatives, and inclusive gameplay.

# Preserve the game while adapting how people play

Read [Designing for games](../../references/designing-for-games.md). Inspect the playable loop, first install, platform/input matrix, display assumptions, and accessibility options. Establish whether the request is a design, review, or port. Keep the engine/framework and game's identity unless the user authorizes a different scope.

Start with time to meaningful play. Include playable material in the initial install, use sensible defaults from the device/accessories/preferences, and teach actions in playable context. Move reference instructions out of the mandatory path. Request permissions when gameplay explains the benefit and ratings after meaningful play. Distinguish measured download time from the guide's target rather than inventing a network result.

For each target platform, map core actions to its normal input before adding controllers. Provide an alternative for players without a controller; watchOS does not share the source's physical-controller support. On touch devices, decide what can be manipulated directly and what needs an onscreen control. Do not copy a pointer game's tiny menus unchanged. Preserve safe areas and text/control readability across aspect ratios and supported orientations; resolve the guide's iOS control-size table/prose tension conservatively at 44 pt for touch rather than silently choosing the smallest value.

Review information channels and difficulty separately. Critical events need alternatives to color/sound alone; subtitles and adjustable mappings/motion/audio can preserve participation without changing the game's purpose. If cross-device progress, multiplayer, haptics, or purchases are in scope, choose relevant Apple integrations after the core loop works rather than adding every service.

**Before → decision → after:** A puzzle port waits for all later worlds to download, teaches through ten text pages, and requires a controller on iPad. Decision: the initial puzzle can teach direct tile manipulation immediately. After, one world ships locally, the first moves teach in context, touch selection and undo cover the loop, and a connected controller accelerates the same actions.

Deliver a revised first-play sequence and per-platform action/display contract or implementation. Fail if the first playable task is unnecessarily blocked, an advertised platform lacks a complete input route, or an essential cue remains single-sense. Report actual engine/device/controller testing separately from static review.

Use [Game controls](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for mappings, [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for accommodations, and [Game Center](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-game-center/SKILL.md) for chosen social play.

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.
---

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Keep the interaction target distinct from the chosen value

Read [Focus and selection](../../references/focus-and-selection.md). Inspect platform/input, focus groups, selected state, dynamic content, and supplied implementation. Establish design/review/adaptation mode. The guide's component-focus model excludes iOS/watchOS; visionOS gaze hover is a different system.

Map focus movement separately from activation and persistent selection. Focus may select automatically only when that does not unexpectedly shift context; tvOS normally needs separate activation. Use system effects and avoid moving focus without input. If an item disappears during discrete directional movement, choose a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide the indicator rather than inventing the next destination.

On iPad, group custom content so Tab moves among logical groups and arrows move within them in expected reading order; prioritize the likely entry item. Ordinary content focus coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls. On TV, every interactive item needs directional reachability and room for enlarged focus art. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, selected, and unavailable states distinct. Full-screen gestures should manipulate visible content rather than invisible focus.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a TV watchlist opens each item as focus passes over it and uses the same glow for focus and Saved. Decision: navigation must not activate content, and persistent choice must survive focus movement. After, focus raises/highlights the item, Select opens it, and a filled saved indicator remains as focus moves; unavailable items are inactive and unreachable.

Deliver a focus-route/group map and state contract or implementation. Walk each entry, direction, activation, return, and removal scenario. Fail if a control cannot be reached/exited, focus jumps without input, selected state vanishes with focus, or enlargement obscures information. Source inspection can establish intended grouping; actual focus engines, remote behavior, and Full Keyboard Access need supported execution.

Use [Remotes](../apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md) for TV button meanings, [Keyboards](../apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for shortcuts/access, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) when the request actually concerns gaze feedback.

name: apple-hig-remotes
description: Use when designing or reviewing tvOS Siri Remote navigation, deliberate activation, playback/scrubbing, Back behavior, or compatible program-guide buttons.

# Preserve deliberate remote actions across browsing and playback

Read [Remotes](../../references/remotes.md). Inspect the TV hierarchy, playback/game state, remote mappings, and requested design/review/adaptation. This is tvOS-specific. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish a remote press from accidental surface contact or movement.

Map swipes to predictable directional focus/scrolling with corresponding feedback; strength can govern scrolling momentum. Use presses for deliberate activation. Avoid acting on taps during live playback because passing or resting a remote can produce them. Press-then-swipe enters scrubbing; preserve the relationship between gesture and visible media position.

Define Back by hierarchy and task state. In ordinary browsing, Back opens the parent, not necessarily the last screen visited; root returns Home. During gameplay, Back may open a pause menu, Back from that menu resumes, and an additional deliberate action can leave for the game menu. Holding Back retains its system Home behavior. Play/Pause must control active media; game-specific secondary/skip use needs appropriate context.

If an electronic program guide exists, guide/browse buttons open it and page buttons navigate it. During playback, those page requests change channels. Without a guide, preserve system routing to the default guide app rather than inventing unrelated meanings.

**Before → decision → after:** A streaming app treats every clickpad tap as Pause and makes Back jump to a recently searched page rather than the show's parent. Decision: accidental touches should not interrupt viewing and hierarchy must remain predictable. After, deliberate Play/Pause controls playback, presses activate, and Back from the episode returns to its show; guide/page behavior follows the active context.

Deliver a state-by-button/gesture mapping and corrected interaction artifact. Walk browse, play, scrub, pause, and return routes. Fail if incidental contact changes playback, Back strands the person or exits unexpectedly, or a program-guide button performs an unrelated action. Actual Siri Remote gestures, momentum, and across-room feedback need hardware testing; keyboard simulation is partial evidence.

Use [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for directional reachability or [Game controls](../apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for controller/menu consistency.

name: apple-hig-onboarding
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting first-use learning, optional tutorials, initial content, and contextual setup requests.

# Get people into a safe first task

Read [the onboarding guide](../../references/onboarding.md). The workflow is application advice; the source adds no separate platform rules.

Inspect the first valuable task, true prerequisites, tutorial/setup flow, permission needs, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Distinguish completed launch from onboarding and unavoidable prerequisites from optional configuration. Record skip persistence and later access from implementation; a Skip button alone is insufficient evidence.

Prefer safe learning through interaction and nearby task-specific tips over memorization slides. Keep prerequisites brief. Optional tutorials must be skippable, remember the decision across launches, and remain accessible later. Package enough initial content for interaction while larger assets download. Postpone optional preferences, permissions, ratings, and purchases until relevant value/commitment; only indispensable private-resource needs justify contextual explanation during onboarding. Integrate unavoidable legal content without derailing learning rather than treating the HIG as authority on legal requirements.

Implement the authorized first-use/skip/resume behavior, provide a prerequisite-versus-optional task flow, or review exact delay and forced-learning defects. Preserve the user's product scope rather than inventing a new multi-step signup funnel.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a drawing app requires six tutorial slides, notification consent, and a rating before opening a canvas; skipped slides return next launch. Decision: learning is blocking value and skip is not respected. After: open a safe sample canvas, introduce one relevant tool in context, postpone unrelated requests, and retain optional tutorial access through Help.

Deliver the artifact, initial task, prerequisite rationale, skip memory, and later-help route. Verify fresh/returning/skipped users, unavailable assets, denied optional permission, and re-entry. Fail for repeated skipped onboarding, optional setup blocking all value, or launch disguised as passive tutorial time. Report actual persistence/device execution separately from flow inspection.

Load [launching](../apple-hig-launching/SKILL.md), [offering-help](../apple-hig-offering-help/SKILL.md), or [managing-accounts](../apple-hig-managing-accounts/SKILL.md) for the affected prerequisite.

# Preserve the playable action across input devices

Read [Game controls](../../references/game-controls.md). Inspect the core action set, target platforms, active controller profiles, touch regions, and requested design/review/adaptation scope. Preserve the engine and separate gameplay bindings from menu navigation. watchOS is unsupported here; controller requirements on tvOS/visionOS need the appropriate store badge and graceful absence handling.

Map the loop to the platform's built-in input first, with controller enhancement where useful. On touch, prefer direct manipulation for objects and virtual controls for movement/many actions. Keep frequent actions near thumbs, outside camera/movement regions and hardware safe areas; use the guide's frequent/secondary size requirements. Show pressed feedback that remains visible around a finger. Label actual actions rather than borrowing arbitrary physical button letters. Combine related actions and avoid complex simultaneous combinations.

Detect active controller/profile and player, updating glyphs accordingly. Outside gameplay, preserve familiar activation, cancel/back, section, selection, and pause mappings; Home/logo stays system-owned. If connection drops or no required controller exists, explain connection and retain a usable state. On keyboards, favor reachable related bindings and customization, while preserving system commands. For visionOS spatial controllers, retain look/trigger indirect and reach/trigger direct semantics.

**Before → decision → after:** A climbing game puts tiny A/X buttons beside the Home indicator and keeps Xbox labels after a different controller connects. Decision: actions need reachable touch controls and labels matching active hardware. After, “Grab” and “Jump” touch regions sit in safe thumb areas with clear pressed states, while connected-controller prompts use that player's actual glyphs; menus retain conventional Back/Pause behavior.

Deliver an action-to-input/player mapping and corrected control layout or implementation. Fail if the advertised platform cannot complete the loop, input changes produce wrong prompts, or a control conflicts with system gestures. Hardware mapping, ergonomics, and multiplayer identity need actual device/controller tests; list unperformed checks.

Use [Designing for games](../../../apple-hig-getting-started/.topics/apple-hig-designing-for-games/SKILL.md) for first-play/platform scope and [Gestures](../apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md) for supplementary touch interaction.

description: Use when choosing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform text hierarchy, system/custom fonts, Dynamic Type, Bold Text, legibility, or spatial text.

# Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

Assign semantic roles before choosing sizes: title, body, supporting detail, and actionable label need a clear relationship. Prefer system text styles and runtime font APIs so optical design/tracking adapt to size. If a custom face is needed, verify weight/legibility and provide equivalent text-size and Bold Text behavior; thin faces may need more size than the table suggests. Use loose leading for sustained/wide reading, avoiding tight leading across three or more lines.

Decide how content expands. Grow containers, permit labels to wrap, stack timestamps/glyphs, and reduce columns rather than aggressively truncating essential reading. Scale meaningful glyphs with the text. Preserve hierarchy while prioritizing the content people intend to read; not every decorative/transient number must grow identically.

Apply platform differences: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so use appropriate standard-control fonts and explicit product text accommodations rather than promising that API behavior. On visionOS, favor readable 2D text, explicit styles for New York, little extrusion, and viewer-facing object labels; do not rely on cast shadows against unpredictable surroundings. Watch uses its own font conventions, including complication typography.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a book list fixes custom thin titles to one line and leaves status glyphs tiny at larger text sizes. Decision: reading and status must remain usable together. After, titles use a legible role/weight, wrap into growing rows, supporting text stacks, and meaningful glyphs scale while selection/actions stay available.

Deliver corrected type roles, resizing rules, or implementation with supported-size examples. Fail if essential content is clipped without a full-text route, hierarchy collapses, or Bold Text/custom sizing breaks controls. Record tested sizes and actual font measurements; device-distance legibility, native shaping, and spatial comfort need supported execution.

Use [Layout](../apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for reflow, [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for task-level access, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for mixed-script alignment.

name: apple-hig-voiceover
description: Use when designing or reviewing VoiceOver names, dynamic values, reading order, grouping, headings/rotor structure, meaningful images/charts, or spatial gesture alternatives.

# Expose the task's structure without relying on sight

Read [VoiceOver](../../references/voiceover.md). Inspect the task, actual accessibility semantics when available, visible content, dynamic updates, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack. A screenshot cannot establish spoken names, rotor behavior, focus order, or successful nonvisual operation; distinguish proposals from inspected runtime semantics.

Name important controls by actual function, improve unhelpful generic labels, and synchronize descriptions/values with changing content. Describe meaningful imagery only for information the image conveys beyond nearby captions; hide decoration from navigation. For charts, expose a concise purpose plus accessible equivalents for every interaction, not merely a label saying “Chart.”

Build navigation structure from the task. Give pages short unique titles and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, links, ordering, and relationships otherwise conveyed by proximity/alignment, following locale reading order and grouping captions with their own images. Mark headings/links for rotor navigation and notify assistive technologies of relevant content/layout changes without inventing untested announcement behavior.

On visionOS, custom-gesture apps do not normally receive hand input while VoiceOver exploration is active. # Explain the entitlement before the purchase

Read [Apple In-App Purchase](../../references/apple-in-app-purchase.md). Inspect what is sold, entitlement duration, existing-customer paths, prices/offers, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the payment stack; use current platform documentation for implementation/eligibility rather than treating this design snapshot as current commercial policy.

Classify the product first: digital goods/features/subscriptions use this model; physical goods/services and donations belong to Apple Pay guidance. Choose consumable, nonconsumable, auto-renewing, or nonrenewing behavior according to what access means. Advanced Commerce needs eligibility, not merely a large catalog.

Show usable value before prompting and keep purchase discovery integrated. Use clear short product names, complete localized billed amounts, and the unmodified system confirmation. For subscriptions, display included service, period, full billing total, any introductory/trial duration, subsequent price and automatic billing, Terms/Privacy, and sign-in/restore for existing purchasers. Keep full totals more prominent than equivalent-period breakdowns; never resell a new subscription to someone who already has access. TV should reduce entry through another device/code; Watch still needs complete terms and an easy close/cancel route.

Define what follows redemption/purchase and how people manage access. Apply entitlements promptly, support prelaunch redemption, explain eligible Family Sharing for purchaser/recipient, and make subscription management/cancellation easy to reach. Purchase help should show useful product/date context and an obvious system refund request; do not promise Apple's refund outcome.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a language app advertises “Only $2/month,” bills annually, hides restore, and shows the same offer to active subscribers. Decision: terms and existing access must be explicit. After, the paywall leads with the full annual charge and period, explains any trial-to-paid transition, exposes sign-in/restore, and routes existing subscribers to content/management instead of repurchase.

Deliver corrected offer/paywall/help states or implementation. Fail if the billed total is obscured, existing purchases cannot be recovered, trial billing is ambiguous, or cancellation/refund access is buried. Static copy review cannot establish StoreKit transactions, entitlement synchronization, eligibility, or refunds; identify sandbox/device checks still pending.

Choose strong automatic defaults from display resolution, connected controllers/accessories, and accessibility settings. Teach controls in playable context; make written instructions a reference rather than a gate. Ask for sensor or personal-data permissions at the moment gameplay explains the need, and request ratings only after meaningful play. ## Look stunning on every display Keep text readable with adequate background contrast. Source default/minimum text sizes are: |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS and iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Keep buttons separated and easy to activate. Respect safe areas, rounded corners, and camera housings. Support distraction-free full screen on phone, tablet, and Mac, and Full Space where suitable on visionOS. ## Enable intuitive interactions Provide the platform’s normal input first and adapt control sizes and menus when moving from pointer input to touch. |Platform|Default input|Additional inputs identified by source| |---|---|---| |iOS|Touch|Game controller| |iPadOS|Touch|Controller, keyboard, mouse, trackpad, Pencil| |macOS|Keyboard, mouse, trackpad|Controller| |tvOS|Remote|Controller, keyboard, mouse, trackpad| |visionOS|Touch, including eye-targeted hand interactions|Controller, keyboard, mouse, trackpad, spatial controller| |watchOS|Touch|None listed| Physical controllers are supported on all these platforms except watchOS, but offer alternative interaction for players who lack or cannot use one. Support varied names, descriptions, avatars, and human characteristics. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. # Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Remotes Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. The Siri Remote combines physical buttons and a touch-sensitive clickpad for tvOS navigation, selection, and playback across the room. ## Best practices Preserve standard gestures and focus direction outside specialized gameplay. Provide clear feedback connecting gesture to content. Presses indicate deliberate activation; resting/moving/passing the remote can cause accidental taps, so avoid acting on taps during live playback. Positional up/down/left/right taps can help only when intuitive and discoverable. Back normally opens the hierarchy’s parent, which is not always the previously visited screen; at the root it returns Home. During play, Back can open a pause menu to avoid accidental exits; Back from that menu resumes, while another deliberate action can return to the game menu. Holding Back reaches Home. Play/Pause must play, pause, or resume active media. ## Gestures Swipe scrolls with momentum based on swipe strength; vertical swipes along an edge accelerate through many items. Press activates or selects, and pressing before swiping enters scrubbing. ## Buttons Touch-surface swipe navigates/changes focus in apps and acts like a D-pad in games. Surface press activates/deepens navigation or acts as the game primary button. Back handles parent/exit or pause/resume according to context. Play/Pause controls media, while games may use it as a secondary action or to skip an intro. ## Compatible remotes For an app with an electronic program guide, guide/browse buttons open it; page-up/down navigate within it, also supported by upper/lower surface taps. Without an EPG, the system sends those requests to the default guide app. While content is playing, page-up/down should change channels rather than page through the guide. ## Platform considerations This source is tvOS-specific and marks the other five platforms unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance.

# Game controls Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/game-controls) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Support a platform’s built-in input even when controllers enhance play: not everyone owns or can use one. All listed platforms except watchOS support physical controllers. ## Touch controls For iOS/iPadOS, use direct manipulation where it fits and TouchController virtual controls when movement or numerous actions require them. Keep common buttons near thumbs, clear of movement/camera areas, Home indicator, Dynamic Island, and safe-area obstructions; put secondary menus higher. Frequent controls need at least 44 × 44 pt, less important ones at least 28 × 28 pt. Give a visible pressed state that remains perceivable under the finger plus appropriate haptic/audio feedback. Depict actual actions rather than arbitrary A/X/R1 labels. Hide irrelevant controls and consider revealing movement controls only on touch. Combine related actions and use hold/double-tap variants instead of demanding complex button combinations. Conventionally left controls movement and right controls camera; maximize their input regions, place a movement thumbstick at the thumb’s landing point, and prefer direct camera panning over a second virtual stick. ## Physical controllers Keep default-input alternatives: touch, keyboard/pointer, remote, or eye/hand gestures. tvOS/visionOS games can require a controller with the appropriate App Store badge, but must gracefully detect absence and request connection. Detect paired controllers and profiles automatically. Show glyphs/labels for the actual active controller and correct player in multiplayer, not framework-generic lettering; symbols usually beat prose for quick recognition. Outside gameplay, map A to activation, B to cancel/back, shoulders to previous/next section, thumbsticks and D-pad to selection, and Menu to settings/pause. Home/logo remains reserved for the system. The source assigns no universal UI action to X, Y, or either trigger. Handle several connected controllers and combined labels when referring to more than one. ## Keyboards Prefer quick single-key bindings, nearby keys for related/frequent actions, and large easy-to-reach keys such as Space for a primary action. Test on Apple keyboards: Command beside Space can be more comfortable than a borrowed Control mapping for WASD play. Provide customization for ability, comfort, and play style. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS rules; watchOS is marked unsupported. ### visionOS For spatial controllers such as PlayStation VR2 Sense, preserve hand-input semantics: look then press either trigger for indirect action, or reach to an object then press a trigger for direct interaction. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/game-controls) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024.

# Onboarding Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Onboarding follows completed launch. Ideally the product teaches itself; when needed, make initial learning quick, enjoyable, and optional. ## Best practices Teach through safe interaction rather than passive instruction. Consider nearby context-specific tips that introduce one task at a time. Any prerequisite flow should stay brief and avoid memorization. Let people skip an optional tutorial, remember that choice across launches, and make it accessible later through help/settings/account areas. Teach the app rather than generic system use. ## Additional content A necessary splash should communicate at a glance without delaying use. Package enough initial content to permit interaction while large assets download. Prefer App Store agreement/disclaimer presentation before download; unavoidable in-app legal content should be integrated without derailing learning. ## Additional requests Use sensible defaults and postpone optional configuration. If private resources are indispensable to any function, onboarding can explain benefits before the permission request; otherwise request at first relevant use. # VoiceOver Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. VoiceOver makes interface and content usable without visual access, including Apple-platform games and Unity experiences using Apple’s plug-ins. ## Descriptions Label every important element, improving generic system labels to describe actual function and labeling custom controls. Keep descriptions synchronized with changing content. Describe meaningful images only for information they themselves convey, avoiding redundant surrounding captions. Give charts/infographics a concise purpose description and accessible equivalents of every interaction. Hide purely decorative imagery from accessibility navigation to reduce irrelevant speech. ## Navigation Give each page a short unique title and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, order, links, and relationships otherwise conveyed only through proximity/alignment. Use the current locale’s reading sequence and group images with their own captions. Notify assistive technologies when visible content or layout changes. Identify headings, links, and other content for rotor navigation; the rotor can also offer braille keyboard access. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### visionOS With VoiceOver enabled, custom-gesture apps do not receive hand input by default, preventing accidental app actions during accessible exploration. A person may enable Direct Gesture mode, which turns off standard VoiceOver gestures and lets the app receive hand input directly. Application advice: do not make custom gestures the only route through the experience. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: March 7, 2025.

# Apple In-App Purchase Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-in-app-purchase) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use In-App Purchase for digital goods, premium features, and digital subscriptions. Apple Pay serves physical goods/services and donations. Consumables deplete and can be rebought; nonconsumables do not expire; auto-renewables continue until canceled; nonrenewing subscriptions require a new purchase to extend time. Advanced Commerce API serves qualifying complex, frequently updated/multicreator catalogs and bundled subscription add-ons; consult eligibility and review rules. ## Best practices Let people experience value before purchase, keeping shopping integrated with app styling. Use short clear names/descriptions and always show the complete billed price. Show a usable store only where payments are allowed, explaining parental/payment restrictions if needed. Use the system confirmation sheet without imitation or modification. ### Supporting Family Sharing Eligible nonconsumables/auto-renewables can be shared with up to five additional family members across devices. Highlight sharing in product names/signup information, explain benefits and the system’s notifications/settings, and tailor copy for both the purchaser and family recipients. ### Providing help Offer missing-purchase help, FAQs, support/feedback, contextual product/date information, and alternatives such as immediate fulfillment, while keeping a clearly labeled refund request readily visible without extra scrolling/screens. Hand off to the system refund flow; do not speculate about Apple’s approval or refund policies. A help link to Apple’s refund explanation is appropriate. ## Auto-renewable subscriptions Explain benefits and terms during onboarding with a clear action. Offer suitable content tiers/durations and sampling via freemium access, metering, or trials. Prompt at meaningful moments and make subscribing generally findable. Do not advertise a new subscription to an existing subscriber; let cross-app/web customers sign in instead of paying again. ### Making signup effortless Give distinct short option names, price/duration, introductory price and period, and subsequent standard price. Ask only essential initial data. On tvOS, use another device/code for entry/authentication. Signup must include subscription name, period, included service/content, localized complete billing amount, sign-in/restore for existing purchasers, and Terms/Privacy links. Put full billing totals above equivalent-period price breakdowns. Clearly state trial length and automatic billing after it. Include signup in settings. ### Supporting offer codes One-time codes from App Store Connect work through redemption links, supported in-app UI, or App Store entry; choose these for restricted/small distributions. Custom reusable codes fit mass campaigns and redeem by URL or supported in-app UI, not App Store account settings. Custom codes use ASCII letters/numbers only. Explain offer terms and redemption clearly. A Redeem Code action should open the system flow; it can appear in paywalls, onboarding, or settings. Optional promotional art replaces the default app icon. Apply unlocked entitlements immediately and welcome people appropriately, including those who redeemed before first launch. ### Helping people manage their subscriptions Show subscription summaries and upcoming renewal near account/settings management. Prefer system subscription UI for upgrade/downgrade/cancel. Relevant alternative plans, discounts, or later win-back offers can help, but cancellation must remain easy to identify and reach. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS rules. ### watchOS Include the same required subscription information while explicitly describing device-specific content/function differences. A modal sheet can present the complete details with a convenient Close; custom flows also need Close/Cancel to free content. Make duration/discount comparisons compact, either separate purchase buttons locked to descriptions or a list plus a clearly labeled purchase button reflecting the chosen option. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-in-app-purchase) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 17, 2026, September 12, 2023, November 3, 2022.

# Typography Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Ensuring legibility](#Ensuring-legibility) - [Conveying hierarchy](#Conveying-hierarchy) - [Using system fonts](#Using-system-fonts) - [Using custom fonts](#Using-custom-fonts) - [Supporting Dynamic Type](#Supporting-Dynamic-Type) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) ## Ensuring legibility Test type at real viewing distances, lighting conditions, and supported devices. Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped. Keep important content toward the top and the overall hierarchy stable. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS SF Pro is standard; New York is also available. ### macOS SF Pro is standard and New York is available to Mac Catalyst apps. macOS has no Dynamic Type. Match standard-control typography with the relevant NSFont methods: `controlContentFont`, `labelFont`, `menuFont`, `menuBarFont`, `messageFont`, `paletteFont`, `titleBarFont`, `toolTipsFont`, `userFont`, `userFixedPitchFont`, `boldSystemFont`, and `systemFont`, each with its `ofSize:` parameter. ### tvOS SF Pro is standard, with New York also available. ### visionOS SF Pro is standard; specify text styles explicitly when using New York. Body/title Dynamic Type styles are bolder, and Extra Large Title 1/2 support wide editorial compositions. Prefer readable 2D text with little or no extrusion. Test full-scale designs through different viewing scales. Default white text contrasts with glass; test custom colors against diverse surroundings. Without a container background, bold can improve visibility; do not rely on unpredictable cast shadows. Billboard labels associated with 3D objects toward the viewer, normally rotating around the y-axis so the baseline stays perpendicular to the line of sight. ### watchOS SF Compact is standard, New York is available, and complications use SF Compact Rounded. ## Specifications Values below preserve the source’s factual measurements. Sizes, leading, and line heights are in points; tracking is given in thousandths of an em and points. Emphasis can be applied through SwiftUI `bold()` or UIKit `UIFontDescriptor` `traitBold`; the resulting emphasized weight varies by style. Use semantic APIs in production instead of freezing all layout to these reference values. ### iOS, iPadOS Dynamic Type sizes #### xSmall |Style|Weight|Size, pt|Leading, pt|Emphasis| |---|---|---|---|---| |Large Title|Regular|31|38|Bold| |Title 1|Regular|25|31|Bold| |Title 2|Regular|19|24|Bold| |Title 3|Regular|17|22|Semibold| |Headline|Semibold|14|19|Semibold| |Body|Regular|14|19|Semibold| |Callout|Regular|13|18|Semibold|

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.
